transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sara Lim (HorizonCare - Procurement), Dr. Amit Patel (HorizonCare - CTO), Liam O'Connor (HorizonCare - Legal), Nina Roy (HorizonCare - VP Eng)

Summary (auto): Procurement/Legal review — went through MSA/DPA high-level redlines, SLA ask (99.9% uptime, p95 latency targets), data residency/KMS concerns, and next steps for pricing approvals and pilot benching.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna (AE): Hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Jenna from Redwood Inference, with me is Marco our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sara (Procurement): Doing well, thanks. We wanted to get through the MSA/DPA redlines and make sure we align on SLAs and the pricing approval path.
[00:12] Marco (SE): Yep, we'll cover all of that. Quick intro on our side, we'll keep it short then go into the contract points and the technical asks for the pilot.
[00:18] Dr. Amit (CTO): Great, our timeline is pretty tight — procurement wants a recommended vendor list by end of month, and security needs SOC 2 and KMS details early next week.
[00:26] Liam (Legal): And I have a few DPA clauses to discuss — data residency, subprocessors, and liability caps.
[00:31] Jenna (AE): Sure, let's start with the MSA. We received your redlines yesterday, we flagged three major areas: liability cap, indemnity carveouts, and termination assistance. On indemnity we can be flexible but need to align on IP carveouts.
[00:44] Liam (Legal): Yeah the IP language is fine, it's the liability cap — your standard cap is one times fees, but with PHI in scope we were hoping for two times or a higher carveout for gross negligence.
[00:55] Jenna (AE): Understood. We'll propose a middle ground in the redlined doc — increase in specific circumstances tied to regulatory fines. I can send that back by Thursday.
[01:03] Sara (Procurement): That'd help procurement move faster. Also on the DPA, the data residency table — we need confirmation we can keep EU patient data within EU regions and a clause that prohibits cross-border processing without notice.
[01:15] Marco (SE): We support region pinning in both Hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments you can keep everything in your VPC on-prem. For hosted we can guarantee EU region processing and include that in the DPA. Note: sometimes the transcription in our internal notes says 'K-V cash' — it's K-V cache, that's what we use for prefix caching.
[01:30] Nina (VP Eng): On the security side, we need to confirm KMS/HSM integrations — we plan to use AWS KMS, but may require a Bring Your Own Key flow.
[01:37] Marco (SE): We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer customer KMS integration with restricted key policies and audit logs. We'll send the integration doc.
[01:46] Dr. Amit (CTO): What about SSO and RBAC? Our directory is Okta.
[01:50] Jenna (AE): SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning is available; RBAC is role-based with admin/ops/readonly roles. We'll include the SSO guide.
[01:58] Liam (Legal): SLA question — we need 99.9% uptime and some latency SLOs for critical inference routes. What do you commit to?
[02:06] Marco (SE): For Hosted tier our SLA is 99.9% with latency targets dependent on model and sequence length. Typically for a mid-size model we can hit p95 ~ 150-300ms on short seqs, but for long 2k-4k token sequences latency goes up. For Dedicated you can get lower tail latency and predictable throughput. We'll capture specific p95/p99 numbers in the SLA appendix.
[02:25] Dr. Amit (CTO): We run a mix of short chat and longer summarization calls, QPS bursty — what's your approach to graceful degradation?
[02:33] Marco (SE): Smart routing and automatic fallback to smaller model variants or regional capacity. Also prefix KV caching and batching helps reduce cost while keeping p95 in check. We'll show benchmarks for your prompt set.
[02:42] Sara (Procurement): Pricing — procurement needs the committed capacity numbers and an example TCO for hosted vs dedicated. Also the approval chain here requires legal + finance sign-off for any 12+ month commit.
[02:52] Jenna (AE): We'll produce a committed capacity proposal with illustrative costs and a 12-month vs on-demand comparison. We'll also highlight the expected unit cost reductions with Dedicated and quantization profiles.
[03:02] Nina (VP Eng): For the pilot we want to run a 2-week POC with 1k QPS spikes, sample prompt set of roughly 200 prompts, and measure p95/p99 and token costs. Can you run that?
[03:12] Marco (SE): Yes, we can run a pilot on a small Dedicated pool or hosted with reserved capacity. We'll instrument token-level cost and latency and share a bench spreadsheet.
[03:21] Liam (Legal): On subprocessors, can you provide a list and the change-notice process? We want 30 days notice for new subprocessors and right to object for critical ones.
[03:29] Jenna (AE): We have a current subprocessors list; we'll include the subprocessors and our change-notice process in the DPA. 30 days is typical, we can agree to a notice plus discussion.
[03:36] Dr. Amit (CTO): One more technical ask — we need a latency benchmark for 4k token sequences (summarization) and the 95th percentile number for both Hosted and Dedicated.
[03:44] Marco (SE): Got it, we'll run a 4k token bench on a representative model variant and provide p95 and cost per 1k tokens. Expect results within 4 business days.
[03:53] Sara (Procurement): For approvals, finance needs an example purchase order and invoice cadence; also want a trial credit applied to the pilot costs.
[04:01] Jenna (AE): We can issue a pilot credit; I'll include sample PO language and invoice cadence options (monthly/quarterly).
[04:07] Nina (VP Eng): Any compliance artifacts — ISO, SOC, penetration test reports?
[04:11] Marco (SE): SOC 2 type II report yes, pen test summary and our infra diagram with VPC/KMS flow. We'll redact sensitive details but provide enough for your security review.
[04:19] Liam (Legal): Liability cap again — can you provide insurance certificate details? We need to route that to procurement.
[04:24] Jenna (AE): Yes we carry E&O and cyber liability; I'll attach certs with the MSA redline.
[04:28] (brief crosstalk)
[04:30] Sara (Procurement): Ok recap please?
[04:32] Jenna (AE): Recap: 1) We'll send redlined MSA/DPA by 2026-05-21 with suggested liability language; 2) Marco will run and share 4k token p95 bench and bench spreadsheet by 2026-05-22; 3) We'll provide SOC2 report, subprocessors list, KMS integration doc by 2026-05-20; 4) HorizonCare to send data residency/KMS preference and sample prompt set by 2026-05-25; 5) Schedule technical deep-dive week of 2026-05-25.
[04:49] Dr. Amit (CTO): That works for us, procurement will start internal approval once the redlines and SOC2 are in.
[04:57] Jenna (AE): Great—thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[05:02] Sara (Procurement): Thanks all.
[05:04] (call ends)
